cohort: 121 pregnancies in 79 SLE patients with and without LN, who attended the Materno Neonatal Hospital in Cordoba city, Argentina, from January 2015 to April 2017
finding: While pregnant SLE patients with LN experienced a higher rate of maternal complications such as lupus flares and preeclampsia, LN did not lead to worse pregnancy and fetal outcomes compared to pregnant SLE patients without LN.
mod_finding: A caesarean section was required in 68.5% of the LN group vs 31.5 in the group without LN, and urgent caesarean section was also performed in the LN group.
